dealNotes: 10-year agreement announced 2017 per Washington Post; financial terms not disclosed. Inova ended partnership in April 2021, approximately 5 years early, citing decision to focus on orthopedic and musculoskeletal growth. Sponsorship as Official Health System continued through 2021 season. Current Commanders health partners include VHC Health (women's health, Oct 2023) and OrthoVirginia (orthopedic/sports medicine, Sept 2022).

financials.source: FY2025 (12 months ended Dec 31, 2025) operating data from Becker's Hospital Review reporting on EMMA continuing disclosure. Total operating revenue $7.3B (+11.5% YoY), net patient service revenue $6.8B (+10.7%). Operating income $582.7M (8.0% margin), up from $366.8M (5.6%) in FY2024. Net income $2.0B (FY2025), $1.3B (FY2024). Non-operating revenue of $1.417B estimated as net income minus operating income, driven primarily by investment returns on $9.5B portfolio. Balance sheet figures (total assets $14.67B, total liabilities $3.58B) from Ernst & Young audited consolidated financial statements as of Dec 31, 2024. FY2024 revenue of $6.55B is estimated from 11.5% growth rate. Obligated group for bond purposes consists of Inova Health System Foundation (EIN 54-1071867) and Inova Health Care Services (EIN 54-0620889). EIN 54-1760205 not found on ProPublica; primary 990 filings are under those two EINs.

balanceSheetWealth.investmentPortfolioSource: EMMA continuing disclosure filing for period ended March 31, 2025. Obligated group investments of approximately $9.5B, of which $7.9B can be liquidated within three days. Asset allocation: global equity 51.6%, fixed income 21.8%, private investments 15.4%, cash 4.2%. Investment Fund comprises ~93% of assets whose use is limited, Capital Fund ~7%. Portfolio managed through internal investment office.
balanceSheetWealth.realEstateSource: Not separately disclosed in consolidated financials; Fairfax County real property assessment records would show individual parcels across five hospital campuses
balanceSheetWealth.notes: Inova Health System maintains one of the largest investment portfolios among U.S. nonprofit health systems. Total net assets grew from $9.71B (Dec 31, 2023) to $11.09B (Dec 31, 2024), a $1.38B increase in one year, driven by investment returns and operating surpluses. The $9.5B investment portfolio is approximately 16x FY2025 operating income of $582.7M. Five hospital campuses across Northern Virginia's Fairfax County, Loudoun County, and City of Alexandria represent substantial real estate holdings in some of the highest-value jurisdictions in the United States.

bondDebt.largestIssueProceeds: Recent issuances include Series 2024 and Series 2022 refunding bonds. Series 2018A/B totaled $500M ($206.86M Series 2018A confirmed). 2022 Loudoun County Board approved up to $425M refunding authority. Proceeds used for Inova Fairfax Medical Campus expansion/renovation, capital equipment, and refinancing of prior series.
bondDebt.priorOutstandingEstimateSource: Becker's/Moody's reference to Aa2 affirmation on approximately $1.15B of outstanding debt (pre-2024 issuance); current total likely higher after Series 2024 issuance
bondDebt.obligatedGroup: Inova Health System Foundation, Inova Health Care Services, Inova Loudoun Hospital, Inova Health System Services, Inova Alexandria Hospital
bondDebt.source: EMMA/MSRB filings, Bond Buyer, Moody's, and Becker's Hospital Review. Bonds issued as tax-exempt healthcare revenue bonds through Fairfax County Industrial Development Authority as conduit issuer. Joint and several general obligation of the Obligated Group. Total liabilities of $3.58B (Dec 31, 2024 audited) include bonds plus other liabilities. Exact current bonds-payable total requires review of audited financial statements debt footnote on EMMA.

communityBenefit.source: REQUIRES LIVE VERIFICATION from Schedule H Part I-II and Virginia Health Information state reports. Lown Institute Hospital Index (FY2020 data) identified Inova as having a fair share deficit — the system received an estimated $218M in annual tax benefits while spending approximately $95M on community investment, a shortfall of approximately $123M. Verify current year from Schedule H.

taxAdvantage.notes: Virginia imposes a 6% corporate income tax. Inova is exempt from federal and state income tax, property tax, and sales tax across five hospital campuses in Fairfax County, Loudoun County, City of Alexandria, and Fairfax City — among the highest-value real estate jurisdictions in the United States. Bond debt generates significant tax-exempt interest subsidy. Lown Institute estimated total annual tax benefits at approximately $218M with community spending at approximately $95M, yielding a fair share deficit of approximately $123M (FY2020 data). Full tax advantage computation requires current property assessments, bond debt figures, and 340B program data.

layoffs.description: System-wide workforce reduction primarily affecting administrative and support roles as part of cost optimization; Inova cited need to reduce expenses amid post-pandemic financial pressures
